content.name: Liam Fitzgerald
content.title: Principal Mechanical Engineer
content.summary: Principal mechanical engineer (CPEng, RPEQ) with 16 years in bulk materials handling, rail maintenance and mining services across Queensland. Leads a team of nine engineers and drafters, and a conveyor upgrade program I directed raised plant availability from 88% to 95%.

experience.title: Graduate Mechanical Engineer
bullets: Supported maintenance engineers on stacker-reclaimers, conveyors and ship loaders at a coal export terminal.
Analysed failure records for conveyor pulleys and idlers, helping move 40 components onto condition-based maintenance.
Prepared engineering change packages and work instructions for shutdown crews.

experience.title: Mechanical Engineer
bullets: Managed bogie and brake system modifications for a fleet of 70 passenger rail cars.
Wrote technical specifications and supervised contractors during overhaul, keeping work within a $3 million annual budget.
Reduced wheel replacement frequency by about 15% after a wheel-rail interface study with the track team.
Achieved Chartered status (CPEng) with Engineers Australia in 2015.

experience.title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
bullets: Led mechanical design for coal handling and preparation plant upgrades worth up to $25 million.
Checked designs against AS 4024 machinery safety and AS 1210 pressure vessel requirements before sign-off.
Registered as an RPEQ in 2017 and certified mechanical designs for Queensland projects.
Ran root-cause analyses on chute blockages that removed about 120 hours of unplanned downtime a year.

experience.title: Principal Mechanical Engineer
bullets: Lead a team of nine mechanical engineers and drafters delivering materials handling and process projects for mining and port clients.
Directed a three-year conveyor upgrade program that lifted plant availability from 88% to 95% for a major client.
Set technical standards and review gates for all mechanical deliverables, and sign off designs as the RPEQ.
Grow and manage a client portfolio worth about $8 million in annual fees.
Mentor graduates and engineers working toward CPEng and RPEQ, with five registered so far.
